title: F1 in Las Vegas: You've never seen an F1 race like this before
gist: The 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix delivered oval-style slipstream racing thanks to new aero rules, long straights, cold track temperatures and negligible tire wear; Max Verstappen won his 75th race while Mercedes and Ferrari self-destructed. Jonathan Gitlin argues F1 should ask Pirelli for different tires, since current high-pressure, overheat-prone compounds suppress close racing.

insights.claim: Under 2026 Formula 1 rules, undersized lithium-ion hybrid batteries deplete quickly on long straights, leaving cars on just over half power with V6 engines running without electric-motor assistance.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Shows energy-management limits of F1's hybrid push, relevant to the motorsport-as-EV-tech-showcase narrative.
insights.quote: the inadequate size of their lithium-ion hybrid batteries means they become depleted very quickly

insights.claim: The 2026 F1 aerodynamic regulations made the slipstream far more powerful than in previous years, producing pack racing at Las Vegas closer to an IndyCar oval race.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: More unpredictable racing improves the product for F1's US commercial expansion.

insights.claim: Las Vegas's cold night-time conditions, with track temperature of 59°F versus potentially over 122°F in the Middle East, combined with concrete streets to give low grip but virtually no tire wear or overheating.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Explains why the Vegas race's excitement is unlikely to be repeated elsewhere.
insights.locator: And because it takes place at night

insights.claim: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli lost a last-lap passing opportunity by accidentally draining his battery entirely instead of charging it, illustrating how hybrid deployment strategy decides 2026 races.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Energy-management software and strategy is now a key competitive differentiator in F1.

insights.claim: Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix, his 75th victory, with McLaren's Lando Norris 0.64 seconds behind and Oscar Piastri a similar gap further back, boosting McLaren against Ferrari in the constructors' fight for second.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Constructors' standings determine prize money allocation among teams.

insights.claim: Mercedes, which clinched the 2026 Constructors' championship in Mexico, left Las Vegas off the podium after George Russell crashed on lap 47 and Antonelli drained his battery.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Shows volatility even for the dominant team under new rules.

insights.claim: Ferrari's intra-team rivalry is costing it points: Charles Leclerc ignored a team order and collided with Lewis Hamilton, earning a 10-second penalty, and the author argues Ferrari should consider benching Leclerc for Qatar.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Ferrari team dysfunction weighs on its constructors' result and brand.
insights.quote: one of Ferrari’s reserve drivers would be getting a call to get ready to replace him for the weekend in Qatar

themes.theme: Tire policy as the lever for better racing

insights.claim: F1 asked Pirelli after the chaotic 2010 Canadian Grand Prix to make tires that replicate that unpredictability, but teams quickly optimized strategies around consistent Pirelli tires, leaving little room for chaos.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Regulatory design choices shape the entertainment value underpinning F1's media and commercial revenue.
insights.locator: F1’s powers that be saw this

insights.claim: Pirelli's F1 tires remain hard to drive on because of mandated high minimum pressures and a tendency to overheat when following another car, and Pirelli has limited Qatar sets to 27 laps.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Tire constraints suppress overtaking, a product issue for F1.
insights.locator: And the Pirelli tires, while better

insights.claim: After Las Vegas, the author argues Formula 1 should ask Pirelli for a different kind of tire to enable closer racing.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Signals potential future tire-spec changes affecting Pirelli's F1 supply relationship.
insights.quote: Pirelli makes the tires that F1 asks for, but after this weekend’s race, it’s time for the sport to ask for something different.
insights.locator: And the Pirelli tires, while better
